reference.title: Dumbbell Straight Arm Pullover
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbell goes back behind the head, exhale as you pull it back over the chest.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.6 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Straight arms make a long lever: start lighter than for a bent-arm pullover.
prescription.progression: More reps, a 1 s pause in the stretch, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie along a flat bench with your head near the end, feet planted. Hold one dumbbell over the chest with both palms cupping the top plate, arms straight.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell in a long arc behind your head, arms staying straight, ribs down.
Stop when the arms are about in line with the body and the lats stretch; the low back stays on the bench.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back along the same arc with straight arms.
Pause with the dumbbell over the chest, then go again.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows on the way down
mistakes.fix: Lock in straight (not hyperextended) arms; the bent-arm pullover is a different exercise.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching off the bench at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs, keep the ribs down and stop the arc where the back stays flat.
Lower slowly; go only as deep as the shoulders allow comfortably.

mistakes.mistake: Loose grip on the dumbbell over the face
mistakes.fix: Cup the top plate firmly with both palms and use a dumbbell with fixed plates.

mistakes.mistake: Head hanging off the end of the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the back of the head on the bench and the neck neutral.

kinematics.setup: Along the bench, top of the head at the end of the pad (-4.8 cm past it)
kinematics.peak: Glutes and upper back on the bench (rig shapes), back of the head just off the pad with a neutral neck
kinematics.norm: Lying along a flat bench, head and hips supported (as in Teixeira 2022, supine on a flat bench); the cross-bench version with only the shoulders on the bench is an alternative (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈177° at the bottom (arms aimed 8° above the line of the back so the dumbbell clears the head)
kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees (arms over the chest) toward 180 degrees (arms in line with the body); Teixeira 2022 tested 0-180 degrees
Straight arms: elbows at about 170-180 degrees (clinical opinion); Pezarat-Correia 2020 kept a slight elbow flexion

kinematics.setup: Both palms on the top plate, dumbbell hanging along the forearms
kinematics.peak: Dumbbell behind the head, lowest point 48.6 cm above the floor
kinematics.norm: One dumbbell, both palms cupping the top plate (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 2.4 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.6 s up, 0.6 s over the chest
kinematics.norm: Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s down and 1.5-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #043312, Dumbbell Straight Arm Pullover, video (movement reference)

Teixeira, Gomes, da Silva, Magalhães and Marchetti 2022, differences between pullover and pulldown exercises on maximal isometric force and myoelectric activity in recreationally-trained men (Int J Exerc Sci 15(4):797-807; PMC9362894)
Pezarat-Correia, Medeiros, Fernandes, Vaz, Silva and Moraes 2020, comparison of shoulder and trunk muscle activation between different pullover exercises (Rev Andal Med Deporte 13(3):127-133)
Campos and Silva 2014, comparison of electromyographic activity during the bench press and barbell pullover exercises (Motriz 20(2):200-205)

cautions: Lie along the bench with the head near its end; get the dumbbell up by holding it on the chest first, then press it over the chest with both hands (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain overhead (for example impingement): keep the arc short or choose another lat or chest exercise (clinical opinion).
Hold the dumbbell firmly over the face; use a fixed-plate dumbbell, never one with loose collars.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Limited overhead mobility: shorten the arc.
Elbow discomfort: allow a slight bend.
progressions: Slower lowering with a pause in the stretch.
Cross-bench pullover (shoulders on the bench, hips low).

muscleNotes.lats_r: Shoulder extensor from overhead; latissimus activity was higher at 135-180 degrees of shoulder flexion than near the chest (Teixeira 2022) and about 44-46% of MVIC across pullover variations in Pezarat-Correia 2020.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Shoulder extensor from overhead; latissimus activity was higher at 135-180 degrees of shoulder flexion than near the chest (Teixeira 2022) and about 44-46% of MVIC across pullover variations in Pezarat-Correia 2020.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Pulls the arms back over the chest in the first part of the lift; the pectoralis was about as active as the latissimus (roughly 43-49% of MVIC) in Pezarat-Correia 2020 and peaked between 90 and 135 degrees of flexion in Teixeira 2022.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Pulls the arms back over the chest in the first part of the lift; the pectoralis was about as active as the latissimus (roughly 43-49% of MVIC) in Pezarat-Correia 2020 and peaked between 90 and 135 degrees of flexion in Teixeira 2022.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: The long head crosses the shoulder and helps extend it (about 46-47% of MVIC in Pezarat-Correia 2020; more active in the pullover than the bench press in Campos 2014); it also holds the elbows straight.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: The long head crosses the shoulder and helps extend it (about 46-47% of MVIC in Pezarat-Correia 2020; more active in the pullover than the bench press in Campos 2014); it also holds the elbows straight.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Controls the shoulder blades as they rotate upward overhead and back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Controls the shoulder blades as they rotate upward overhead and back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps extend the shoulder; similar activity to the latissimus in Pezarat-Correia 2020.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps extend the shoulder; similar activity to the latissimus in Pezarat-Correia 2020.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the dumbbell, both palms cupping the top plate.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the dumbbell, both palms cupping the top plate.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down: the low back should not arch as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help keep the ribs from flaring as the arms reach overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help keep the ribs from flaring as the arms reach overhead.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Steady the shoulder blades on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Steady the shoulder blades on the bench.
